methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $356M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Gatik, a Series C autonomous transportation company founded by Gautam and Arjun Narang, has raised $356M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of eight private frontier-tech firms in transportation, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

The stage-progression method is applicable and drives the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised ($356M) as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C progression to the next stage yields $605M. The peer-median method was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the transportation sector—only three peers exist in the broader category, but none met the filtering thresholds of stage proximity or valuation tier alignment. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce excessive noise.

The triangulated valuation range is $514M to $695M, with a median implied value of $605M. This range reflects the sensitivity around stage-progression assumptions and the inherent uncertainty in a single-method analysis. Key risks to valuation include the absence of narrow peer benchmarks, execution risk inherent to pre-commercial autonomous platforms, and capital intensity typical of the sector. The median estimate should be viewed as provisional pending additional comparable data or revenue/unit economics visibility.
